reason: Conversation 1 gives a coherent, honest diagnostic path: it recognises the unit is probably a static fridge, explains the full defrost (switch off, towels, keep food cold), and flags the 10C food-safety risk. It says plainly that a sealed-system fault is an engineer job and that the landlord or agent should arrange it, with a written report. It does overreach somewhat by leaning toward a sealed-system fault from the freezer at -16C, and it never asks for the model label. Conversation 2 asks repetitive questions, assumes a fan or defrost drain the homeowner has said they cannot see, and suggests 'keep doors shut 24 hours' as a fix. It also repeats the drain question after the user had said there is none, never suggests a full defrost, and gives no food-safety warning, though it does correctly steer toward reporting to the agent.
